examples.title: Split full nodes before descending
examples.explanationHtml: Minimum degree two permits three keys per node. Splitting a full root promotes its middle key and increases the height.

examples.title: Search several keys within each page
examples.explanationHtml: The search compares against each sorted key in a page before selecting the child interval containing 17.

examples.title: A leaf-chain range scan in a small B+ layout
examples.explanationHtml: Separators 10 and 20 choose a starting leaf. Following next links then emits 7, 10, 12, 17 and 20 without returning to the root.

practice.title: B-tree membership
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12), insertion keys (-99..99), then an int query. Use minimum degree two and set semantics. Print Count and keys: then found=0 or 1.
hints: Stop at an equal key before choosing a child.

practice.title: Report the root page
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12) and insertion keys (-99..99). Build a minimum-degree-two B-tree by splitting full nodes before descent. Print Count and keys: then root: and its sorted keys.
hints: A root split creates a new internal root.

practice.title: Count stored B-tree keys
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12) and insertion keys (-99..99), ignoring duplicates. Print Count and keys: then keys=C counting keys in internal pages as well as leaves.
hints: Promoted keys still belong to a B-tree.

practice.title: B-tree range query
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12), insertion keys (-99..99), and int low/high with low at most high. Print Count and keys: then range: with inclusive matching keys in sorted order.
hints: Visit internal keys between their surrounding children.

quiz.prompt: Why do disk indexes favor wide search-tree nodes?
options: One page read can choose among many child intervals
Disk pages store only one key
quiz.explanation: High fan-out reduces the number of page levels visited.

quiz.prompt: With order m defined as maximum children, how many keys can a full internal node hold?
quiz.explanation: Sorted keys separate one more child interval than the key count.

quiz.prompt: In a minimum-degree-two B-tree, what is the maximum keys per page?
quiz.explanation: The maximum key count is 2t-1 with t=2.

quiz.prompt: When a full B-tree root splits, what happens to leaf depth?
options: Every leaf becomes one level deeper
quiz.explanation: A new root sits above the old root halves.

quiz.prompt: Where are full data records kept in the B+ convention used here?
quiz.explanation: Internal separators guide search; linked leaves hold the records.

quiz.prompt: What should a B+ range scan do after locating its first leaf?
options: Restart at root for every key
Follow next-leaf links until the upper bound is passed
quiz.explanation: The leaf chain gives consecutive record ranges in order.

quiz.prompt: Does B-tree insertion use AVL single rotations as its basic repair?
options: No, it splits full nodes and promotes keys
quiz.explanation: A B-tree balances page occupancy and equal leaf depth through splits.

quiz.prompt: A full t=2 page has keys 5, 10, 20. Which key is promoted by its split?
quiz.explanation: The middle key at index one is 10.

quiz.prompt: With maximum fan-out four, how many keys separate those child intervals?
quiz.explanation: Four ordered intervals need three separating keys.

quiz.prompt: The lower-bound search stays on the current page. Which child interval contains query 17?
quiz.explanation: Seventeen exceeds 10 but precedes 20, selecting child interval one.

keyPoints.bn: বি-ট্রির এক পেজে সাজানো একাধিক কী থাকে।

keyPoints.bn: এই লেসনে অর্ডার m মানে সর্বোচ্চ mটা চাইল্ড।

keyPoints.en: Splitting promotes a middle key to the parent.

examQuestions.question: For minimum degree two, insert 10,20,5,6,12,30,7,17. Give all root splits and the final pages.
examQuestions.answerHtml: After 10,20,5 the leaf root is [5,10,20]. Before inserting 6, split it into root [10] with leaves [5] and [20]; insert 6 into the left leaf. Later the right leaf [12,20,30] splits before 17 is inserted. Final root is [10,20] with leaves [5,6,7], [12,17] and [30]. All leaves remain one edge below the root.

examQuestions.question: Define order as maximum children. For order four, give internal non-root key and child limits and explain the root exception.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A non-root internal page holds 2..4 children and 1..3 keys. A leaf also holds 1..3 keys but has no children. An internal root has at least two children; the empty tree may use a leaf root with zero keys. The exception permits small trees before the first split.

examQuestions.question: Compare a B-tree split with a B+ leaf split and explain the effect on range scans.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A B-tree moves the middle key into the parent, and records may appear in internal pages. A B+ leaf split keeps full records in leaves and copies a boundary separator upward. Linked B+ leaves then allow a range scan to descend once and continue along next links. An ordered B-tree scan must include internal keys as well as leaf keys.

examQuestions.question: For B+ leaves [5,6,7] -> [10,12,17] -> [20,30], trace inclusive range [7,20].
examQuestions.answerHtml: Route lower bound 7 to the first leaf using separators 10 and 20. Skip 5 and 6, emit 7, follow next and emit 10,12,17, then follow next and emit 20. Stop when 30 exceeds the high bound. The result is [7,10,12,17,20], with no repeated root descent for each record.

summary.en: Use wide nodes for page access and understand splits and linked-leaf range scans.
summary.bn: চওড়া নোডে বেশি কী রেখে পেজ পড়া কমাও, আর নোড স্প্লিট ও লিফ ধরে রেঞ্জ সার্চ বোঝো।
